weekend_summary: Spa returned Antonelli to winning form after two difficult rounds. He started from pole, briefly lost the lead to Verstappen, then retook it and later had to chase Leclerc after Ferrari gained a cheap stop under a short VSC. Antonelli passed Leclerc with roughly 10 laps remaining and won by under two seconds. Russell's race ended early after contact with Hamilton, while Verstappen completed the podium. The weekend also exposed Aston Martin's severe pre-Hungary deficit and featured several grid penalties that complicate raw start-to-finish comparisons.

Q.summary: Antonelli took a dominant pole, with Verstappen closest; Norris qualified near the front but carried a 10-place grid penalty.

key_moments.text: Antonelli started from pole with Verstappen alongside.
Norris' 10-place power-unit penalty moved him down the official grid.

R.summary: Antonelli won after retaking the lead from Verstappen early and later chasing down Leclerc, who had gained track position through a VSC-assisted stop.

key_moments.text: Verstappen swept past Antonelli at Eau Rouge on Lap 1, but Antonelli reclaimed the lead quickly.
Hamilton and Russell made contact early, sending Russell into the gravel and out of the race.
A short VSC allowed Leclerc to gain track position through a cheaper stop.
Antonelli caught and passed Leclerc late to win by 1.952s.

ANT.name: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
ANT.summary: Antonelli's Spa win was a strong recovery statement: he overcame both an early loss of track position and a later strategy disadvantage to pass Leclerc on track.

details.text: This makes the victory a stronger pace/execution signal than a simple inherited win.

LEC.name: Charles Leclerc
LEC.summary: Leclerc used the VSC to jump Antonelli during the stop cycle and then forced Mercedes to win the race back on track.

details.text: P2 by less than two seconds shows Ferrari remained a genuine race-winning threat.

RUS.name: George Russell
RUS.summary: Russell's race ended in an opening-lap collision with Hamilton after he had already lost deployment and fallen backwards.

details.text: The DNF is not a usable measure of his race pace.

VER.name: Max Verstappen
VER.summary: Verstappen briefly took the lead and finished third, showing front-running race pace even though he could not sustain Antonelli's pace over the full event.

details.text: His podium was Red Bull's third of the season at that point.

ALO.name: Fernando Alonso
ALO.summary: Aston Martin arrived at Spa at the low point of its season and was badly off the midfield pace, sharpening the importance of the B-spec due in Hungary.

details.text: The team's own pre-Hungary comments described the Spa deficit as roughly two seconds to the midfield and more than four seconds to the Q1 benchmark.

Mercedes.summary: Mercedes had a split weekend: Antonelli delivered a mature win while Russell scored zero after the opening-lap collision.

details.text: Team-level averages should not treat Russell's DNF as pace weakness.

Ferrari.summary: Ferrari remained close enough to use strategy to lead and force Antonelli to pass Leclerc late.

details.text: Hamilton finished fourth despite serving a penalty for the Russell contact.

Aston Martin.summary: Spa exposed the depth of Aston Martin's chassis deficit immediately before its planned Hungary B-spec.

details.text: That baseline is important when interpreting the size of any Hungary improvement.

VCARB.summary: Racing Bulls brought a meaningful package but could only allocate it to one car initially, creating a driver-scoped rollout rather than a clean two-car comparison.

details.text: The team publicly discussed the practical limitation of only having enough parts for one car at Spa.

strategy_and_conditions.text: A short VSC materially altered the lead battle by giving Leclerc a cheaper stop.
Several drivers carried grid penalties, so official starting position and qualifying pace should be kept separate.

performance_interpretation.text: Antonelli's win is strong evidence of Mercedes race pace because he had to recover a strategy disadvantage and pass Leclerc on track.
Russell's DNF and Norris' grid penalty make final positions poor standalone pace measures for those drivers.

prediction_review.overall_assessment: No genuine saved pre-race LatentLap forecast exists for this round. Do not reconstruct one retrospectively and label it as an original forecast.

knowledge_limits.text: Actual ERS deployment and battery state are not public; LatentLap's energy-management signals remain inferred, not measured.
Race-session harvest ratios are not used as reliable comparative evidence because representative laps differ in fuel, compound and track evolution.
Stint pace trends are fitted lap-time slopes over filtered green-flag laps, not direct tyre-degradation measurements; fuel burn, traffic, track evolution and driver management can contribute.
The presence of a new component at a weekend does not prove it caused an observed pace change. Upgrade effects are only attributed where reviewed reporting explicitly supports an effect.
